title: Jane Eyre
synopsis: Gateshead, Lowood, Thornfield. You are small and plain and on fire on the inside. The master of the house has, you'll learn, a wife in the attic.

nodes.text: Bewick's Birds, rain, cousin John throws a book.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Defend yourself” back. Spirit shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Wise—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: Locked in. Faint at midnight.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Brave.
“Sleep” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Honest.

nodes.text: He looks at you the way a wolf looks.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Hold your gaze” back. Spirit shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Cold porridge. Helen Burns reads Rasselas.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Heart.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Go.” The story records the instinct as “Path” and carries it forward.
You commit to “Stay.” The story records the instinct as “Honest” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: The house is ruins. He, blinded, lives at Ferndean.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Find him.” The story records the instinct as “Path” and carries it forward.
“Walk away” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Honest.
Some endings reveal themselves last.

nodes.text: You marry him at Ferndean. He regains sight in one eye in time to see your first child. You live, plainly and devotedly, for many years.
You open a small school for girls on your inheritance. You teach them, among other things, that a small plain girl can refuse a wrong life and find a right one.
You write a book under another name. It is, in places, your life. It is, in many homes, kept on a shelf at the level of the eye.
